text:
‘Piggyback,’ said my cousin, while

barberized, barberized, barberized

he walked along our street

with a little suitcase under his arm

and still feeling widowed

from the companion of his life

the other funeral guests had come too

the double cast of mourners

with lingerie crepe over rose-colored lips

but he passed me with a dissolving face

and greeted me like someone

who, just as so many times before,

takes upon himself once more

the world's great surge

in his little boat of solitude.


Now then, dear ants, how are you?

Do you like being here in this flourishing land?

You never rest, for what suits you best is

to swarm according to the plan whispered to you

violet faces, round heads, doll eyes

Roman cut on a fine blond cranial type

lying down with Schubert songs, listening on the plush ramp

strawberry cheeks

turn around completely so

your whole figure can be seen

turn back, live; a smile is not enough

a glance emerging from behind the shop windows

or the tender touch of two eyes set far apart

but you must head

toward the dance, temptation, entanglement

you will go on step by step

or stop and stand motionless:

someone will always come to help you out

of the fix

but it takes a long time to realize

what should have happened and what did happen

then one stops again and holds one's breath

or hums a song or

begins to love jazz.
